hypotheses.statement: An improper exception request for G1 leaves the evidence state SECURED, is recorded as applicability REJECTED with an open exception proceeding, and cannot be accepted
The ledger keeps every proceeding opened for a case; the single-state variant keeps one
Completing one proceeding does not complete or erase another

targets: receipts, evidence, proceedings, plans, measurements and closures of a synthetic ledger

reproduction.world: xzr.teoo.lawledger (SQLite, append-only) on xzr.teoo.lawworld (8 Booleans); this implementation's own world, not Appendix O

L201.criterion: E stays SECURED, A is REJECTED, the exception proceeding is open, the evidence is unchanged and the exception cannot be accepted, in every world

L202.contrast: proceedings kept per world: ledger minus single state

L203.criterion: completing one proceeding leaves the other open, in every world

catalogue.source: The Minimum Guarantees of Human Legal Subjecthood, Publication Final V3.0, Chapter 6.2 (identical in the 100_POINT_EDITION and in R2 section 4: all fifteen titles and definitions compared character for character)
catalogue.note: V3.0 uses two vocabularies for the same five findings (Appendix A table: Secured/Partial/Absent/Indeterminate/Inapplicable; A.3 and 8.4 text: Satisfied/Partially Satisfied/Failed/Indeterminate/Not Applicable). R2 section 16 and this implementation use the table's.

note: results about a SYNTHETIC ledger and this implementation's own world; the manuscripts R5-R16, the historical code and the world of Appendix O were not available and their numbers are not reproduced; a closure, a measurement or a match here is not a legal judgment or a restoration; not an observation of any institution, law or person
